lower_bound.quote: **Lemma 1.** Let $\mathcal A$ be a pairwise-intersecting family of finite sets. Then $\mathcal A$ has only finitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals, that is, finite sets meeting every member of $\mathcal A$ and minimal with this property.
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample: take distinct symbols $u_1,u_2,\ldots$ and $A_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\cup\{u_n\}$. The family $\mathcal A=\{A_n:n\ge1\}$ is pairwise intersecting since every $A_n$ contains 1. For every $k\ge2$, $X_k=\{u_1,\ldots,u_{k-1},k\}$ is a finite minimal transversal: it meets $A_n$ through $u_n$ when $n<k$ and through $k$ when $n\ge k$; deleting $u_j$ makes it miss $A_j$, while deleting $k$ makes it miss $A_k$. Thus there are infinitely many distinct minimal finite transversals.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The proof invokes Lemma 1 to deduce that there are finitely many bounded-cardinality terminal members. As written, that deduction is placed under this false lemma, and no separate valid bounded-size sunflower argument is supplied.

parsed.notes: Mapping: reduction is the greedy support/self-duality reformulation and periodic counting conditional on finite C; lower_bound is finiteness of bounded minimal supports via Lemma 1; upper_bound is strict weight descent from each occurring prime to a bounded terminal support.
